Pensions and retirement benefits · Nigerian complaint guidance

Pension complaints: retirement benefits, unpaid contributions and records

Organise employment records, pension statements and administrator correspondence before reporting delayed benefits or missing retirement contributions.

By PetitionDesk Editorial Team · Reviewed 25 August 2026

Who this guide is for: Employees, retirees or beneficiaries affected by delayed pension benefits, missing contributions, incorrect records or unresolved retirement verification.

Understand the problem before writing

A pension complaint may involve an employer, pension fund administrator, pension fund custodian, government pension department or the administrator of an older pension arrangement. Start by establishing which institution controls the missing record, contribution or benefit decision. Similar terminology does not mean every pension body has the same responsibility.

For missing contributions, compare payslips, the retirement savings account statement, employment dates and any employer remittance information. Explain which periods appear absent and ask the responsible organisation to reconcile the records. A deduction on a payslip and a credited pension contribution should not be treated as identical without evidence.

Retirement benefit delays require the date of retirement, benefit application, verification status, relevant account reference and communications from the administrator. If a beneficiary is acting on behalf of a deceased or incapacitated person, establish the authority to make the request before sharing sensitive records.

Different pension schemes and public-service arrangements may have different administrators. Identify whether the matter belongs to a pension fund administrator, the National Pension Commission, the Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate or another verified authority before choosing an escalation route.

Build an evidence checklist

Use records that relate directly to your complaint. Put events in date order, identify the organisation involved, and keep copies of every message or acknowledgement. Describe what your documents actually show; do not present an allegation as a proven finding.

  • Employer, pension administrator and relevant scheme
  • Employment, retirement or benefit-application dates
  • Retirement savings account or pension reference
  • Payslips, pension statements and remittance records
  • Administrator correspondence and complaint reference
  • Evidence of authority where a beneficiary is acting

Choose the institution that can respond

Address the administrator, employer or pension office that controls the record or payment being challenged. Identify the missing contribution period or disputed benefit decision and request a documented reconciliation or status update.

A company mentioned in a statement, address, receipt or background document is not automatically the institution responsible for the complaint. Identify who provided the disputed service, who made the decision, and who can supply records or correct the problem.

Decide whether escalation is justified

Where the responsible administrator does not resolve the complaint, consider the authority that regulates or administers the particular pension arrangement. Include the earlier complaint, application reference, relevant employment records and the specific outstanding issue.

Before escalating, keep the original complaint reference, the institution's written answer where available, and a concise explanation of what remains unresolved. Check the current instructions published by the relevant authority instead of assuming that one deadline applies to every type of complaint.

Worked example: applying the route in practice

A retired officer whose administrator has not processed a benefit application should state the retirement date, application reference, documents submitted, administrator response and the precise decision or information still outstanding.

Avoid common mistakes and protect personal data

Do not publish your full identity number, complete pension account credentials or another beneficiary's private records. Avoid assuming that every pension delay is controlled by the same national agency.

Remove passwords, one-time passcodes, card security codes and unrelated medical, financial or family information. Request a specific remedy supported by your evidence, such as an explanation, correction, investigation, refund or written decision.

Frequently asked questions

Who should receive a missing pension-contribution complaint?

Begin with the employer or pension administrator responsible for the missing remittance or statement and preserve the request before considering a regulator escalation.

Are all government pension complaints handled by PenCom?

Not necessarily. The appropriate route depends on the type of pension arrangement and the institution responsible for administering it.

Official sources and contact starting points

These links point to the organisations' published websites or complaint resources. Check that the channel and procedure remain current before sharing your complaint or evidence.
